copy.headline: Pilot stabs captain on Israel-bound flight, and passengers avert a crash

standard.text: A Flydubai Boeing 737 MAX 8 with 180 passengers, flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, sent a distress signal on Wednesday morning and then the code for a hijacking or other unlawful interference. It was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia and landed shortly after 09:00 Danish time; all passengers are safe.

The co-pilot stabbed the captain, and pilots travelling as passengers landed the plane, Israeli authorities say. Benjamin Netanyahu says a pilot has been arrested and is being questioned by the Saudi authorities, and that he apparently tried to crash the plane.
Passengers broke into the cockpit, eyewitnesses say. One of them, a plumber named Yaniv, grabbed the control stick and did what he had seen on television, witnesses tell DR.
Netanyahu says it could have become a new 9/11, and an Israeli minister quoted by TV 2 calls it jihadist terror. The motive is still unclear.

short.text: The co-pilot of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv stabbed the captain on Wednesday; pilots among the passengers landed the plane in Saudi Arabia, and Netanyahu says a pilot has been arrested.

copy.headline_short: Passengers stop cockpit attack on Israel-bound plane
copy.deck: The plane landed in Saudi Arabia; Netanyahu says the pilot has been arrested.

copy.headline: Seven parties get six months to agree on the future of pig farming

standard.text: The government on Wednesday presented the terms of reference for the grisefirepart, a four-party body in which seven parties are to agree on the future of pig farming, chaired by Jacob Bundsgaard, the former Aarhus mayor. Work starts in 2027 and has six months, to the end of June 2027; if the parties cannot agree, the government is ready to take the necessary initiatives, the terms of reference say.

The temporary stop on new conventional pig farms stays in place. Christian Rabjerg Madsen, the minister for nature and animal welfare, says Denmark sends more pigs on long transports than it slaughters at home, but the law will set no numbers.
Danish piglets travel more than diplomats, Lars Løkke Rasmussen told the press conference.

short.text: Seven parties have six months from 2027 to agree on the future of pig farming under Jacob Bundsgaard; if they cannot, the government is ready to take the necessary initiatives.

copy.deck: If they cannot agree, the government is ready to act on its own.

copy.headline: Russia summons Denmark's ambassador over the Gedser helicopter incident

standard.text: Russia has summoned Rolf Holmboe, Denmark's ambassador, in answer to Denmark summoning Russia's envoy after a flare from the frigate Soobrazitelny passed 10 to 15 metres from a Danish Fennec helicopter off Gedser on 14 September.

Vladimir Barbin, Russia's ambassador to Denmark, has written to Ritzau that the helicopter acted 'provocatively'. Jeppe Bruus, the defence minister, rejected that account, noting that the frigate did not contact the helicopter before firing.
'We must not let ourselves be intimidated,' Lars Løkke Rasmussen, the foreign minister, told TV 2 News on Wednesday, saying the Russians will not be able to produce evidence for their version.

short.text: Russia has summoned Denmark's ambassador over the Gedser helicopter incident; 'We must not let ourselves be intimidated,' Lars Løkke Rasmussen says.

copy.deck: Løkke says Denmark will not be intimidated.

copy.headline: Ethics council wants to end anonymous sperm and egg donation

standard.text: Det Etiske Råd, the ethics council, recommended on Wednesday that anonymous donation of sperm and eggs be abolished, so that every donor-conceived child can learn the donor's identity if it wishes. Fourteen of its 15 members back the recommendation, and the minister has called in the parties.

Since 2012 people in fertility treatment have been able to choose between anonymous and open donation. Technology means anonymity can no longer be guaranteed, says Ayo Wahlberg, a council member and anthropology professor.
Ole Schou, director of the sperm bank Cryos, rejects the recommendation and warns that without enough donors such children will not be born.

copy.headline: Evening electricity gets dearer as winter tariffs start

standard.text: Most grid companies switch to winter tariffs on Thursday, 1 October, so the time of day matters more for what households pay to have power delivered. Grid charges more than double, and the rise is far steeper east of the Great Belt than in the rest of the country.
Power used between 17:00 and 21:00 becomes dearer. In the dearest hours the switch raises the electricity bill by an average of 131 per cent.

short.text: Winter grid tariffs from Thursday more than double the charge for delivering power in the busiest hours, most of all east of the Great Belt.
